subject.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions

question: Should caller-owned context-overflow recovery be a supported public `createAgentSession` capability, or remain internal to the embedded runner that owns the corresponding recovery lifecycle?
rationale: The patch’s core bug fix is plausible, but publishing this option defines a lasting plugin SDK behavior and changes who is responsible for recovery outside the one caller that implements it today.

options.title: Internalize recovery ownership
options.body: Keep the existing session SDK contract and pass the embedded-runner-only recovery choice through an internal construction path or internal session config.

options.title: Adopt a public SDK contract
options.body: Retain the option only with explicit API documentation, compatibility tests, and defined recovery obligations for every external caller that selects `caller`.

recommendation.title: Internalize recovery ownership
recommendation.body: Keep the existing session SDK contract and pass the embedded-runner-only recovery choice through an internal construction path or internal session config.

likelyOwner.reason: The current contributor has traced and implemented the relevant recovery boundary, while current-main historical ownership was not independently available.
